text: US stocks rallied in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session on Friday as tech rebounded, with the S&P 500 up 1.6% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq up 2.3% to 24,129.50 and the Dow up 1.2% to 50,774.94. Chip and AI shares led the gains after erratic swings earlier in the week, and the S&P 500 finished the week up about 5.6%, its best week since April 2025, with the Nasdaq up about 6.7%. The TSX closed up 1.20% at 34,839.87 on broad-based buying. In Europe the STOXX 600 rose 1% to 643.85 and the FTSE 100 gained 0.8% to 10,698, while in Asia the Nikkei rose about 2.0%, the Hang Seng about 2.1%, the Kospi 4.2% and the Shanghai Composite 3.2%; a DAX close could not be confirmed.
mood: A broad rebound in AI and chip stocks lifted markets worldwide, though oil swings tied to Middle East tensions and planned US tariff hikes kept some caution in place.

veqt.t: S&P 500 +1.6%, Nasdaq +2.3%, Dow +1.2%, led by a rebound in chip and AI stocks.
TSX rose 1.20% to 34,839.87 on broad-based buying.
STOXX 600 +1% to 643.85 and FTSE 100 +0.8%, with the Nikkei up about 2.0% and the ASX 200 up 0.8%; the DAX close was not confirmed.
Hang Seng rose about 2.1%, Kospi 4.2% and Shanghai 3.2%; Hang Seng Tech was not confirmed.
